NEOMORPH: A structure, part, or organ developed independently, that is, not derived from a similar structure, part, or organ, in a pre existing form.
NAVIGEROUS: Bearing ships; capable of floating vessels. [R.] Blount.
NOMARCH: The chief magistrate of a nome or nomarchy.
NOVITIOUS: Newly invented; recent; new. [Obs.] Bp. Pearson.
NEOCLASSIC ARCHITECTURE: All that architecture which, since the beginning of the Italian Renaissance, about 1420, has been designed with deliberate imitation of Greco-Roman buildings.
NOCTURN: 1. An office of devotion, or act of religious service, by night. 2. One of the portions into which the Psalter was divided, each consisting of nine psalms, designed to be used at a night service. Hook.
NEWFANGLENESS: Newfangledness. [Obs.] Chaucer. Proud newfangleness in their apparel. Robynson (More's Utopia).
NINCOMPOOP: A fool; a silly or stupid person. [Law] An old ninnyhammer, a dotard, a nincompoop, is the best language she can afford me. Addison.
NOVICESHIP: The state of being a novice; novitiate.
NEATNESS: The state or quality of being neat.
NORFOLK SPANIEL: One of a breed of field spaniels similar to the clumbers, but shorter in body and of a liver-and-white or black-and-white color.
NOGGEN: Made of hemp; hence, hard; rough; harsh. [Obs.] Johnson.

NONNITROGNOUS: Devoid of nitrogen; as, a nonnitrogenous principle; a nonnitrogenous food. See the Note under Food, n., 1.

NEURILITY: The special properties and functions of the nerves; that capacity for transmitting a stimulus which belongs to nerves. G. H. Lewes.
NECROMANTIC: Conjuration. [R.] With all the necromantics of their art. Young. Of or pertaining to necromancy; performed by necromancy. -- Nec`ro*man"tic*al*ly, adv.
NORTHING: 1. (Surv. & Navigation) Distance northward from any point of departure or of reckoning, measured on a meridian; -- opposed to Ant: southing. 2. (Astron.) The distance of any heavenly body from the equator northward; north declination.
NAUPLIUS: A crustacean larva having three pairs of locomotive organs (corresponding to the antennules, antennæ, and mandibles), a median eye, and little or no segmentation of the body.
NOMOLOGY: 1. The science of law; legislation. 2. The science of the laws of the mind; rational psychology. Sir W. Hamilton.
NUTGALL: A more or less round gall resembling a nut, esp. one of those produced on the oak and used in the arts. See Gall, Gallnut.
NONCONFORMITY: Neglect or failure of conformity; especially, in England, the neglect or refusal to unite with the established church in its rites and modes of worship.
NIBLICK: A kind of golf stick used to lift the ball out of holes, ruts, etc.
NOTORIETY: The quality or condition of being notorious; the state of being generally or publicly known; -- commonly used in an unfavorable sense; as, the notoriety of a crime. They were not subjects in their own nature so exposed to public notoriety. Addison.
NOMENCLATURAL: Pertaining or according to a nomenclature.
NOTORHIZAL: Having the radicle of the embryo lying against the back of one of the cotyledons; incumbent.

NONEXECUTION: Neglect or failure of execution; nonperformance.
NARRATE: To tell, rehearse, or recite, as a story; to relate the particulars of; to go through with in detail, as an incident or transaction; to give an account of. Syn. -- To relate; recount; detail; describe.
NESTFUL: As much or many as will fill a nest.
NATIONALISM: 1. The state of being national; national attachment; nationality. 2. An idiom, trait, or character peculiar to any nation. 3. National independence; the principles of the Nationalists.
NONDESCRIPT: Not hitherto described; novel; hence, odd; abnormal; unclassifiable. A thing not yet described; that of which no account or explanation has been given; something abnormal, or hardly classifiable.
NAPHTHYLAMINE: One of two basic amido derivatives of naphthalene, C10H7.NH2, forming crystalline solids.
NECROLOGIC: Of or pertaining to necrology; of the nature of necrology; relating to, or giving, an account of the dead, or of deaths.
NITRANILINE: Any one of a series of nitro derivatives of aniline. In general they are yellow crystalline substances.
NURSEMAID: A girl employed to attend children.
NAVAJOES: A tribe of Indians inhabiting New Mexico and Arizona, allied to the Apaches. They are now largely engaged in agriculture.
NONINFLECTIONAL: Not admitting of, or characterized by, inflection.
NAPPING: 1. The act or process of raising a nap, as on cloth. 2. (Hat Making) A sheet of partially felted fur before it is united to the hat body. Knight.
NURSLING: One who, or that which, is nursed; an infant; a fondling. I was his nursling once, and choice delight. Milton.
NOBODY: 1. No person; no one; not anybody. 2. Hence: A person of no influence or importance; an insignificant or contemptible person. [Colloq.]
NICHED: Placed in a niche. "Those niched shapes of noble mold." Tennyson.
NORMA: 1. A norm; a principle or rule; a model; a standard. J. S. Mill. 2. A mason's or a carpenter's square or rule. 3. A templet or gauge.
NEIGH: 1. To utter the cry of the horse; to whinny. 2. To scoff or sneer; to jeer. [Obs.] Neighed at his nakedness. Beau. & Fl. The cry of a horse; a whinny.
NIHILITY: Nothingness; a state of being nothing.
NOSED: Having a nose, or such a nose; -- chieflay used in composition; as, pug-nosed.
NOISY: 1. Making a noise, esp. a loud sound; clamorous; vociferous; turbulent; boisterous; as, the noisy crowd. 2. Full of noise. "The noisy town." Dryden.
NERITINA: A genus including numerous species of shells resembling Nerita in form. They mostly inhabit brackish water, and are often delicately tinted.
NEEDLEWORK: 1. Work executed with a needle; sewed work; sewing; embroidery; also, the business of a seamstress. 2. The combination of timber and plaster making the outside framework of some houses.
NENE: The Hawaiian goose (Branta sandvicensis), state bird of Hawaii and crossword superstar.
